sources.title: Resolution 12189 of 2026: Colombian short-stay exemption for Israeli nationals
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia / Colombian Official Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual official compiled resolution read, including Israel's explicit short-stay exemption, waiver list, repeal of Resolution 8558, publication in Diario Oficial 53.614 on 3 September, and operative next-day commencement. The ministry's compilation identifies 4 September 2026.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Rige a partir del 4 de septiembre de 2026

sources.title: Consolidated Resolution 5488: short-stay conditions and permitted duration
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia / Colombian Official Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual consolidated Article 3 read. Israel is named under the amended List A. No paid local services or wages are allowed under this waiver; Migración Colombia issues the applicable permission. The paragraph defines the short stay as less than 90 days and extension up to 180 only in cases permitted by the rules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: cuya duración es menor de 90 días y que puede ser extensible hasta 180 días

sources.title: Colombian Foreign Ministry confirms ordinary-passport tourist scope
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual 11 September ministry notice explicitly confirms ordinary-passport tourism in both directions and identifies Resolution 12189. Use Colombia's legislated duration wording for the Colombian direction, not the distinct twelve-month visitor limit described here for Colombians going to Israel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: los titulares de pasaportes ordinarios de ambos países que viajen con fines turísticos

policies.title: Israeli ordinary passports: Colombia short-stay visa exemption
policies.summary: Colombia's Resolution 12189 restored visa exemption for Israeli short visitors from 4 September 2026, including ordinary-passport tourism. Migración Colombia determines the permission and actual stay at entry.
conditions: Short-stay activities under this exemption must not generate pay for services, salary or wages in Colombia. Employment, residence and other long-stay purposes are separate.
The consolidated resolution defines a short stay as less than 90 days. Any extension requires separate eligibility and approval; the visa exemption is not an extension.

allowedStays.label: Short stay under 90 days; extension only if permitted
notes: The immigration authority determines the actual period at entry. This does not establish a nationality-specific extension limit.

conflicts.explanation: The currently applied eVisa category predates Colombia's domestic repeal and explicit restoration of ordinary short-stay visa exemption for Israel on 4 September 2026.
